label: Necklines, sleeves and silhouettes
description: Named garment necklines, collars, sleeve shapes, silhouettes, waist placements and hems.
notes: Individual construction features belong here, each phrased as a noun phrase after a garment with. clothing.fabric owns the cloth and object.pattern owns surface motifs; garment names and complete outfits belong in neighboring clothing lists. A value changes one feature rather than bundling a neckline, sleeve and silhouette together. Period construction details remain usable in contemporary clothing without era or presentation restrictions.

values.look: Two curved lobes meet in a dip at the center of the chest.
A wide, shallow opening runs almost horizontally between the shoulders.
A straight lower edge meets upright sides, framing the chest in a square.
The front rises toward straps that fasten behind the neck, leaving the shoulders exposed.
Loose fabric falls into soft, curved folds below the neck.
Two diagonal edges meet in a pointed dip at the chest.
A deep, rounded U-shaped opening curves below the collarbones.
The upper edge runs below both shoulders, leaving the collarbones exposed.
One shoulder is covered while a diagonal upper edge leaves the other bare.
The opening sits close to the base of the neck with little chest exposed.
A small enclosed oval or teardrop opening sits just below the neck.
A deep, narrow opening drops well below the upper chest.
Sheer fabric extends above an opaque bodice, making its upper edge appear to float.
The bodice ends across the upper chest with no shoulder straps.
A small flat collar has rounded ends that meet at the front.
Two crisp triangular points fold outward from a short band around the neck.
A short upright band circles the neck without turned-down points.
A continuous rounded fold runs around the neck and down the front opening.
A broad flat collar forms a square flap at the back and tapers toward the chest.
A ring of tightly gathered or pleated fabric projects outward around the neck.
Folded lapels meet the collar in distinct triangular notches at the upper chest.
Long sleeves billow loosely before gathering into close cuffs at the wrists.
Rounded volume swells at the upper arms, gathered at the shoulder and sleeve edge.
Tiny sleeves project just over the shoulder without covering much of the upper arm.
Sleeves widen steadily toward open, flared cuffs.
Diagonal seams run from the neckline to the underarms instead of circling the shoulder.
Very deep armholes flow from the torso into sleeves that narrow toward the wrists.
Large, inflated upper sleeves narrow sharply into fitted forearms.
Open armholes expose the shoulders and arms without any sleeve fabric.
Short, loose flounces fall from the shoulders in rippling, open folds.
Rounded sleeves balloon around the middle and taper at both the shoulder and cuff.
A rounded puff at the shoulder joins a long, closely fitted lower sleeve.
Overlapping curved sleeve panels form a small split like two flower petals.
Openings expose the tops of the shoulders while fabric still covers the upper arms.
Fitted upper sleeves flare dramatically from the elbow into wide cuffs.
A narrow upper shape widens gradually toward the hem like the sides of a capital A.
The body fits closely through the knees before flaring into a broad lower skirt.
A long, narrow outline falls almost straight from the shoulders or bust to the hem.
A short, flared overskirt projects outward from the fitted waist.
Diagonal grain lets the cloth skim the body and fall in long, fluid ripples.
Extra width and length make the garment hang loosely beyond the body's outline.
Straight sides and a broad upper shape create a squared outline with little waist shaping.
Stretch fabric follows the bust, waist and hips closely with almost no loose volume.
A fitted bodice and waist open into a distinctly full skirt.
Fabric swings outward from the shoulders in a broad tent shape without a fitted waist.
Rounded volume through the torso and hips tapers back inward near the hem.
A full skirt curves outward below the waist and gathers back into a narrower, tucked-under hem.
The waist seam sits directly below the bust, with fabric falling loosely beneath it.
The waist seam sits low on the hips below a lengthened bodice.
The bodice and lower garment meet at the body's narrowest waist point.
The waist seam dips into a pointed V at the center front.
Fabric gathers above a cinched band, leaving a ruffled upper edge.
Overlapping front panels pull diagonally into a tied or fastened waist.
The front edge ends noticeably higher than the longer back edge.
Uneven pointed corners hang below the rest of a loose, draped hem.
A row of rounded curves shapes the lower edge.
The lower edge slopes or steps unevenly from one side to the other.
The garment ends unusually high, leaving a gap above the waist or ankle.
The lower edge reaches the ground, hiding most or all of the feet.
Extra length trails behind the wearer across the ground.
